agent_note: Prose fiction, not verse. This book carries TWO narrating strands and the quotes show both plainly: (a) third-person past-tense narration centred on Myron (q01183, q01191, q01192, q01198), and (b) a first-person narrator writing in the present tense (q01195 'I might be good at what I do... I do not possess an invisibility cloak', q01196, q01197) who also uses 'my cousin Rhys' in q01189. That is a strand split, not diary form -- recording narrating_situation as dual so the two positions are not silently merged. Event count is small (9) and near-even (5 past / 4 present), so this book should go to SPLIT_REVIEW rather than a confident label. q01189 is the single quote most likely to flip the split: it opens in past narration but its bulk is future-tense prediction from a present narrating moment; reading it as present makes the split 4 past / 5 present.
